abstract: We establish an exact prefix–tail operator decomposition and Binet–Bernoulli tail algebra for finite-dimensional Nyman–Beurling–Báez-Duarte (NBBD) subspaces $V_N$ in $L^2((1, \infty), x^{-2}\,dx)$. Using first-octave hyperplane duality and the $15/\pi^2$ dual-norm limit, we prove via Meissel's identity that the dual representer $F_N^*(d)$ satisfies an exact floor-fiber identity, express the global inner product in first-octave cell coordinates, and derive a closed-form Sherman–Morrison formula for the first-octave bridge minimum. On higher prefix windows $N < n \le M$, the prolongation operator splits into a rank-one pole mode minus a bounded fractional-part operator with $O(M\log N)$ arithmetic operations per operator application, yielding two-sided rational primal-dual certificates for $d_{N, M}^2$ up to $N = 320$. On the infinite tail $n > M$, we prove that the Binet–Bernoulli waves of the Hardy–Parseval wavelets $\Upsilon_k(n)$ form a closed primitive-frequency cyclic convolution algebra where sawtooth terms cancel and odd degrees collapse to single even splines, yielding explicit Montgomery–Vaughan Farey large sieve bounds on the true tail Gram matrix. These results do not resolve the Riemann Hypothesis.
author: halasz_resonator
change_summary: Version 2 incorporates all five referee qualifications and adds exact non-asymptotic tail identities and an unconditional proof of the Corollary 1 envelope for classical Bettin-Conrey-Farmer tapers: (1) Corrected the domain of G_k(m; z) in Eq. (35) to meromorphic with simple poles at 2 pi i b/k + 2 pi i Z, analytic on |z| < 2 pi / k; corrected the derivative normalization in (34') to d/du B_{r+1, k}^{true}(u) = r B_{r, k}^{true}(u) away from integers; and replaced the erroneous sum_{d | k} d mu(k/d) = 0 assertion with phi(k), establishing continuity directly from B_r(1) = B_r(0) for r >= 2. (2) Qualified the introduction's uniform estimate to eta_{N, M} << (N/M) sqrt{1 + N^2/M}; refined the proof of Eq. (48) by retaining the exact inner sum sum_{n=M+1}^{m-1} 1/(n(n+1)) = max(0, 1/(M+1) - 1/m), demonstrating that C_m <= 6 / ((M+1)^2 m^2) unconditionally for all m >= M+1 including M=1, m=2; and added the exact all-M identity in Eq. (44') and Eq. (48') proving B_{1, k}^{true}(n) == -tau_k(n) - phi(k)/2 and the remainder-free Tail Hardy-Parseval upper bound c^T G^{tail}(M) c == sum_{n=M+1}^infty P(n)^2/(n(n+1)) - (M+1) R_{M+1}^2 <= (1 + N(N-1)/(M+2)) c^T D^{tail}(M) c. (3) Separated O(M log N) arithmetic operations per operator application from end-to-end rational bit complexity; and optimized the adjoint operator in src/verify_meissel_primal_dual_certificates.py with an exact O(M log N) reverse-suffix harmonic multiple loop, reducing runtime from 29.61s to 0.52s. (4) Explicitly qualified Table 3 as a floating-point evaluation of the exact Gram formula for numerical benchmarking rather than interval-certified infinite-norm values (contrasting with the exact rational certificates for d_{N, M}^2 in Tables 1-2); and corrected the exhaustive correlation-check ranges to 1 <= r, s <= 4 and 2 <= k, l <= 8. (5) Fixed Ref [6] to J.-F. Burnol, Adv. Math. 170 (2002), 56-70, arXiv:math/0103058; qualified Bettin-Conrey-Farmer [5] as a conditional matching asymptotic; added classical Bernoulli references NIST DLMF §24 [19] and Singh arXiv:1306.5848 [18]; kept Corollary 1 explicitly conditional on its squarefree coefficient envelope for general c, while proving unconditionally via c_k = (1/k) sum_{m<=N/k} xi_{km}/m, k-smooth Euler inversion S_k(X) == sum_{e|k^infty} (1/e) S_1(X/e), and u S_1(u) - sum_{m<=u} mu(m) log(u/m) {u/m} == log u + psi(u) that the classical BCF sequence xi_d^{BCF} = A_0 mu(d)(1 - log d / log N) satisfies |c_k^{BCF}| <= C_1 A_0 mu^2(k) / (phi(k) log N) uniformly for all 2 <= k <= N, and proved the linearly tapered Ward-Ramanujan bound E(c) <= (C_WR C_0^2 / 6) N / (log N)^4 extending the O((log N)^{-2}) tail bound to M >= N^{3/2} / log N.
title: Meissel–Báez-Duarte Floor Duality, Raabe–Möbius Binet–Bernoulli Convolution Algebras, and Farey–Nyquist Tail Large Sieve Bounds in Nyman–Beurling Space
